_about: Code-scanning alerts a session read and judged false positives. platform/ci/security_alerts.py moves an open alert listed here out of the 'take next' list of the security-alerts queue into a 'Triaged, awaiting dismissal' section, so later runs stop re-triaging it; the owner dismisses it on the alert page (sessions have no security-events scope). An entry applies only while number, rule and path all match the open alert, so a reused number or a moved finding comes back to the queue. Add an entry only after reading the flagged code; give the reason in a sentence a reviewer can check. Never list an alert to avoid fixing it.

false_positives.reason: results.txt and summary.json hold solver statistics and hypothesis verdicts; the script reads no credential (its only environment read is WORKERS), the 'secret' source is a name heuristic.
A test writes a synthetic invoice with a public example BIC/IBAN to a TemporaryDirectory to check the CLI does not print them; no real account data exists.
Same as #2: synthetic test IBAN written to a temporary file so the test can assert the CLI redacts it.
Same as #2: synthetic remittance reference and IBAN in a temporary file, for a redaction test.
training_audit.json holds aggregate counts, shares and versions from the public NLSY79 release; no respondent-level row or identifier is written.
The bundle is model coefficients, odds ratios and tercile aggregates; no couple-level record is written.
The step summary gets the rendered review; find_secrets returns only (path, pattern name), never the matched text, so no secret value can reach the file.
Invite codes use crypto.randomInt(ALPHABET.length), which is unbiased (rejection sampling); there is no modulo of random bytes.
Every user value in the row's innerHTML goes through escapeHtml (& < > " '); the select options come from constant presets, and the saved value is only compared, never interpolated.
Every interpolated value in the periodic-service row goes through escapeHtml (& < > " ').

resultsReportHtml escapes name and note with esc(), accepts the logo only as https or an image data URI, and the colour only as 6-digit hex (src/lib/resultsReport.ts); the route also sits behind admin auth and the report key.

Only the file path and the secret pattern's name leave find_secrets(): result['secrets'] is [{'path','kind'}], never the matched text, so nothing secret is printed or written. CodeQL taints the word 'secret' in the field name.

The printed problems name workflow secrets and the regex that a value-shaped string matched (check(): '/{rx.pattern}/'), never a secret value; secret values are never read by this script, only names in workflow files.
Prints validation errors for the public, tracked models.yaml; it holds product names and prices, no credentials. The 'proprietary' list it is tainted by is product slugs from LICENSING_TRANSITION.md.
Prints a billing plan table built from the public models.yaml and LICENSING_TRANSITION.md (product slugs and prices); no credential or personal data reaches it.

Intended behaviour. The CLI's whole job is to print a defect report about the invoice the user passed in, to the user's own terminal or --output file. The invoice's own fields (e.g. account numbers) appearing in that report is the product working.

Intended behaviour. --name and --skip are documented as REGEX flags for a local developer CLI; the pattern comes from the person running it, in their own process, so there is no other party to attack.

Intended behaviour. --name and --skip are documented as REGEX flags for a local developer CLI; the pattern comes from the person running it, in their own process, so there is no other party to attack.

Intended behaviour. skipLayers is the user's own 'Ignore layers matching' regex, typed into their own browser tab or passed to the CLI as --skip-layers; it is never stored or read from a URL, so a bad pattern can only slow the user's own tab.

esc() escapes commas as \, because that is WooCommerce's importer format for list cells (explode_values replaces '\,' before splitting); the importer has no backslash escape, so doubling backslashes as CodeQL suggests would corrupt values that contain one.
The sink is an .src set from picture(i); an image src cannot run script (javascript: URLs do not execute in img), and alt/textContent are set as text, not HTML.

packetHtml() escapes every string from the #d= design (esc() on names, labels, notes, the perspective URL) and colours go through hex(), which emits only digits. Probed 2026-11-25 with an payload in every string field: it appears only entity-escaped.
The sink is a download link's href set to URL.createObjectURL(blob) for a file the user built; a blob: URL from this page is not attacker-controlled.

Intended behaviour. status-keeper is a certificate-expiry monitor: it must complete the handshake to read an expired, mismatched or untrusted certificate and report it. No data is sent over the socket, and checkTls fails the check on socket.authorized === false in strict mode (the default).
False positive. text.includes(PLACEHOLDER_ORIGIN) is a build check that the placeholder origin https://example.invalid never ships in a built page; it is not a URL allow-list and authorises nothing.

False positive. body.includes(PLACEHOLDER_ORIGIN) in a test records whether a built file still holds the placeholder origin https://example.invalid/, so the test can fail on it; it is not a URL allow-list and authorises nothing.

The printed rows are public Census County Business Patterns aggregates (establishment and employee counts per NAICS code and state) read from the Bureau's published flat file; the 'private' source is CodeQL's name heuristic matching the 'state' key and the zip-file path, and no personal or secret data reaches the print.
